concepts.explanation: Calibration means measuring the reference disk before every run. It must read ten units; otherwise, stop the run.
The baseline is the measurement of an empty tray. Record it before adding a sample, and do not substitute a sample measurement for it.
Replication means performing the same trial procedure three times under the same recorded conditions. Keep each result separate in the notebook.
An anomaly is a difference above four units between a result and the baseline. Flag it for review rather than silently discarding the result.

summary.text: Before each run, measure the reference disk; it must read ten units or the run is stopped. Record the empty-tray baseline before adding a sample.

During a trial, record sample temperature every thirty seconds for three minutes, keeping the interval consistent. Replicate the same procedure three times under the same recorded conditions and keep results separate.
A result more than four units different from the baseline is an anomaly: flag it for review rather than silently discarding it.
